title: Topology & Geometry by Dr Tadashi Tokieda
why: This is the primary source for the companion. It fixes the order of ideas, the paper-strip demonstrations, the recurring pictorial method, and the level of explanation the site is trying to preserve.
use_carefully: The playlist is supported here by auto-captions, not official lecture notes. One video still lacks recovered captions, so source claims must stay tied to available transcript evidence.

title: TIB AV-Portal series record for Topology & Geometry
why: This records the same AIMS course as an institutional video series. It gives the companion a second source page for course identity: speaker, title, institutional host, series order, and access trail.
use_carefully: Use it to verify identity and access, not to infer extra mathematics. A catalog record can say what course this is; it cannot supply theorem details, missing-caption content, proof order, or lecture-specific wording.

title: Henri Poincare, Analysis Situs and its supplements
why: These papers sit in the historical source line for topology as the study of spaces through preserved structure. For this companion, their job is to anchor the whole-space question: which facts belong to the completed carrier rather than to one drawing?
use_carefully: They are not beginner lecture notes and they are not evidence that Tokieda cited a specific sentence. Use them after the course object is plain: surface, allowed change, preserved account, and claim boundary.

title: Heinz Hopf, Vektorfelder in n-dimensionalen Mannigfaltigkeiten
why: Hopf's paper is a primary reference for the vector-field-index thread behind Poincare-Hopf: local singularities of a field are added and compared with a number belonging to the whole manifold.
use_carefully: The paper is technical and historically downstream from earlier surface intuition. The companion should first explain the arrow field, isolated defects, local turning, and same-surface total before pointing readers to the paper.

title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
why: Hatcher gives a modern route into homotopy, homology, quotient spaces, and invariants. For this site, its job is to show how the course's plain actions become reusable tools: identify points, move paths legally, and protect counts.
use_carefully: It is broader and more algebraic than Tokieda's course. Link it only after the lecture page has already explained the route, gluing rule, deformation, or count in everyday terms.

title: John Milnor, Topology from the Differentiable Viewpoint
why: Milnor's notes connect manifolds, degree, fixed points, and vector-field ideas in a compact differentiable-topology setting. For this companion, they clarify why prepared local conditions can carry whole-space conclusions.
use_carefully: The text assumes more mathematical preparation than the companion. Use it only after the everyday explanation has named the object, legal move, local condition, and global count or existence claim.

title: Victor Guillemin and Alan Pollack, Differential Topology
why: This reference explains generic position, transversality-style thinking, intersection counts, and the route from local smooth data to global topological conclusions. Its course-facing job is to justify the cleanup before signs are trusted.
use_carefully: It belongs in the reference layer because it is more formal than the lecture treatment. The site should first say what meeting was cleaned, what sign rule became available, and why the count survives.
